title: A Tug-of-War Between Static and Dynamic Memory in Intel SGX
problem: Intel SGX enclaves balance static memory (allocated at enclave creation) and dynamic memory (allocated at runtime). Improper allocation strategy causes significant performance degradation due to expensive page management operations.
motivation: SGX is increasingly used for security-sensitive cloud applications. Understanding and optimizing static/dynamic memory allocation can dramatically improve SGX application performance.
method: Harmony measures how different static/dynamic memory allocations affect application performance by running the application and monitoring its behavior. Based on these measurements, it identifies which memory should be allocated upfront (static, avoiding runtime overhead) versus allocated on-demand (dynamic, more flexible but slower). It then recommends a near-optimal split between these two approaches.
key_novelty: Using runtime measurements to optimize the balance between static and dynamic memory allocation achieves 68% latency improvement over purely dynamic allocation and 29% over purely static allocation.
contributions: Analysis of static vs dynamic memory allocation impact on SGX performance
68% latency improvement vs purely dynamic allocation
29% latency improvement vs purely static allocation
limitations: Evaluation limited to SGX applications on Intel processors. Applicability to other TEE implementations (ARM TrustZone, AMD SEV) not explored. Profiling overhead not discussed.
primary_theme: Memory optimization for trusted execution environments
